questions.question: Pipes A and B can empty a full tank in 5 hours and 12 hours respectively. Pipe C can fill the same empty tank in 2 hours. If all the three pipes are opened together, then the tank will be filled in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A empties tank in 5 hours

Pipe B empties tank in 12 hours

Pipe C fills tank in 2 hours

**Formula used:**

Work rate = 1 ÷ Time

Net rate = Filling rate − Emptying rates

Time = 1 ÷ Net rate

**Calculation:**

⇒ Rate of A = −1/5

⇒ Rate of B = −1/12

⇒ Rate of C = +1/2

**Use LCM of 5, 12, 2 = 60**

⇒ Convert each rate to denominator 60

⇒ A = −12/60

⇒ B = −5/60

⇒ C = +30/60

⇒ Net rate = (30 − 12 − 5) / 60

⇒ Net rate = 13 / 60

⇒ Time = 1 ÷ (13/60)

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 13 = (60)/(13)

**∴ The tank fills in 60/13 hours **

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours, and another pipe can fill the same tank in 8 hours. If both pipes are opened at the same time, how long (in hours, rounded off to one decimal place) will it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by the first pipe to fill the tank = 6 hours

Time taken by the second pipe to fill the tank = 8 hours

Both pipes are opened simultaneously.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work / Time taken

Combined efficiency = Efficiency of first pipe + Efficiency of second pipe

Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Work / Combined efficiency

**Calculation:**

LCM of 6 and 8 = 24. Let the Total Work (capacity of the tank) = 24 units.

Efficiency of the first pipe = 24 / 6 = 4 units/hour.

Efficiency of the second pipe = 24 / 8 = 3 units/hour.

Combined efficiency when both pipes are open = Efficiency of first pipe + Efficiency of second pipe = 4 + 3 = 7 units/hour.

Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Work / Combined efficiency = 24 / 7 hours.

⇒ 24 ÷ 7 ≈ 3.42857... ≈ 3.4 hours.

**It will take approximately 3.4 hours to fill the tank if both pipes are opened at the same time.**

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 9 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 63 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be two-third filled, is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by the filling pipe (Pipe A) to fill the tank = 9 hours.

Time taken by the emptying pipe (Pipe B) to empty the tank = 63 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work / Time Taken

Net Efficiency = Efficiency of filling pipe - Efficiency of emptying pipe (when working together)

Time = Total Work / Net Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let the total capacity of the tank (total work) be the LCM of the time taken by the individual pipes.

LCM(9, 63) = 63 units.

Efficiency of the filling pipe (Pipe A) = 63 / 9 = 7 units/hour.

Efficiency of the emptying pipe (Pipe B) = 63 / 63 = 1 unit/hour.

When both pipes are opened simultaneously, the net efficiency of filling the tank is:

Net Efficiency = 7 - 1 = 6 units/hour.

Two-third of the total work = (2/3) × 63 = 2 × 21 = 42 units.

Time taken to fill two-third of the tank = Amount of work to be done / Net Efficiency

Time = 42 / 6 = 7 hours.

**The time in which the tank will be two-third filled is 7 hours.**

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill the tank in 60 hours and 90 hours, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will 75% of the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fills the tank in 60 hours

Pipe B fills the tank in 90 hours

We need to find the time taken to fill 75% of the tank when both pipes are opened together.

**Calculation:**

Assume LCM of 60 and 90 as total capacity of tank = 180 units

Work done by Pipe A in 1 hour = 180 ÷ 60 = 3 units

Work done by Pipe B in 1 hour = 180 ÷ 90 = 2 units

Combined work in 1 hour = 3 + 2 = 5 units

75% of 180 units = (75/100) × 180 = 135 units

Time required = Total work / Work per hour

Time = 135 ÷ 5 = 27 hours

**∴ The tank will be 75% filled in 27 hours **

questions.question: A tap can fill a tank in 8 hours. After half the tank is filled, four more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A tap can fill a tank in 8 hours.

After half the tank is filled, four more similar taps are opened.

**Formula used:**

Rate of filling = Work done per hour

Time = Work ÷ Rate

**Calculation:**

Time taken by 1 tap to fill the tank = 8 hours

Rate of 1 tap = 1 ÷ 8 (tank/hour)

Time to fill half the tank with 1 tap = 1 ÷ 2 × 8 = 4 hours

Remaining tank to be filled = 1/2

With 5 taps (1 original + 4 additional):

Rate of 5 taps = 5 × (1 ÷ 8) = 5/8 (tank/hour)

Time to fill the remaining half tank:

⇒ Time = Work ÷ Rate

⇒ Time = (1/2) ÷ (5/8)

⇒ Time = 8/10 = 0.8 hours

⇒ 0.8 × 60 = 48 minutes

Total time to fill the tank:

⇒ 4 hours (first half) + 0.8 hours (second half)

⇒ 4 hours + 48 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is option (2): 4 hours, 48 minutes.**

questions.question: Two inlet pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 30 minutes and 36 minutes, respectively. Initially, only A is opened for 10 minutes. After 10 minutes, A is closed and B is opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the inlet pipe B fill the remaining part of the cistern?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A can fill a cistern in 30 minutes.

Pipe B can fill a cistern in 36 minutes.

Pipe A is opened for 10 minutes initially.

After 10 minutes, A is closed and B is opened.

**Calculation:**

Total Work (LCM of 30 and 36):

Prime factorization of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

Prime factorization of 36 = 2² × 3²

LCM(30, 36) = 2² × 3² × 5 = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180 units (Total Capacity of the cistern)

Efficiency of Pipe A (EA) = Total Work / Time taken by A = 180 / 30 = 6 units/minute

Efficiency of Pipe B (EB) = Total Work / Time taken by B = 180 / 36 = 5 units/minute

The work done by Pipe A in the first 10 minutes = 6 units/minute × 10 minutes = 60 units

Remaining Work = Total Work - Work done by A = 180 - 60 = 120 units

Time taken by B = Remaining Work / EB = 120 units / 5 units/minute = 24 minutes

**∴ Inlet pipe B will fill the remaining part of the cistern in 24 minutes.**

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 18 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 21 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be filled is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A pipe can fill a tank in 18 hours.

Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 21 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Net part filled in 1 hour = (Part filled by the first pipe in 1 hour - Part emptied by the second pipe in 1 hour)

**Calculation:**

Part filled by the first pipe in 1 hour = 1/18

Part emptied by the second pipe in 1 hour = 1/21

Net part filled in 1 hour = (1/18 - 1/21)

To subtract these fractions, we need a common denominator:

LCM of 18 and 21 = 126

⇒ 1/18 = 7/126

⇒ 1/21 = 6/126

Net part filled in 1 hour = (7/126 - 6/126)

⇒ Net part filled in 1 hour = 1/126

Therefore, the time required to fill the tank is the reciprocal of the net part filled in 1 hour:

Time required = 1 / (1/126)

⇒ Time required = 126 hours

**The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: Two pipes X and Y can fill a cistern in 21 hours and 24 hours, respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously, and it is found that due to a leakage in the bottom it takes 48 minutes more to fill the cistern. When the cistern is full, in how much time will the leak empty it if no pipe is open during that time?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe X fills the cistern in 21 hours.

Pipe Y fills the cistern in 24 hours.

Due to leakage, it takes 48 minutes (48/60 = 4/5 hours) more to fill the cistern.

**Formula used:**

Work done = Rate × Time

Rate of filling = 1 / Time taken to fill

**Calculation:**

Rate of pipe X = 1/21 (cistern/hour)

Rate of pipe Y = 1/24 (cistern/hour)

Combined rate of X and Y = 1/21 + 1/24 = (8 + 7) / 168 = 15/168 = 5/56 (cistern/hour)

Time taken by X and Y without leakage = 1 / (5/56) = 56/5 hours

Time taken with leakage = 56/5 + 4/5 = 60/5 = 12 hours

Let the rate of leakage be 1/L (cistern/hour), where L is the time taken to empty the full cistern.

Combined rate of X, Y, and leakage = 1/21 + 1/24 - 1/L = 1/12

5/56 - 1/L = 1/12

1/L = 5/56 - 1/12 = (15 - 14) / 168 = 1/168

L = 168 hours

**∴ The leak will empty the full cistern in 168 hours.**

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 1000 litres in 5 hours and 6 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 1800 litres?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Pipe A fills 1000 L in 5 hr = 1000/5 = 200 L/hr

Pipe B fills 1000 L in 6 hr = 1000/6 = 500/3 L/hr

Combined rate = 200 + 500/3 = 1100/3 L/hr

Time for 1800 L = 1800 ÷ (1100/3) = 5400/1100

⇒ Time = 54/11 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

Pipe A can fill the tank in 5 hours.

Pipe B can fill the tank in 6 hours.

Capacity of the tank = 1000 litres.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A and B together in 1 hour = Work done by A in 1 hour + Work done by B in 1 hour

Time taken to fill the tank together = Total capacity / Work done by A and B together in 1 hour

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 1 hour = 1000 / 5 = 200 litres/hour

Work done by B in 1 hour = 1000 / 6 = 166.67 litres/hour

Work done by A and B together in 1 hour = 200 + 166.67

Work done by A and B together in 1 hour = 366.67 litres/hour

Time taken to fill 1800 litres = 1800 / 366.67

Time taken to fill 1800 litres = (1800)/(366.67)

Time taken to fill 1800 litres = (1800 × 3)/(1100)

Time taken to fill 1800 litres = (5400)/(1100)

Time taken to fill 1800 litres = (54)/(11) hours

**The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 37(1)/(2) minutes and 45 minutes, respectively. Both pipes are open. The cistern will be filled in just half an hour, if the B is turned off after:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can fill the cistern = 37.5 minutes = 75/2 minutes

B can fill the cistern = 45 minutes

**Concept used:**

Total work = Efficiency of a person × Time

**Calculation:**

Taking the L.C.M. of 75/2 & 45 = 225 (which is total work)

Work done by A in 75/2 minutes = 225

Efficiency of A in 1 minute = (225 × 2)/75 = 6

Work done by B in 45 minutes = 225

Efficiency of B in 1 minute = 225/45 = 5

Let the turned off time of B be x minutes.

Efficiency of A in 1 minute × Time + Efficiency of B in 1 minute × Time = Total work 

⇒ 6 × 30 + 5 × x = 225

⇒ 180 + 5x = 225

⇒ 5x = 225 – 180 

⇒ x = 45/5

⇒ x = 9 minutes

**∴ B is turned off after 9 minutes.**

questions.question: A tap can fill a tank in 6 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken to fill half the tank by 1 tap = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 hours.

The remaining half of the tank is filled by 4 identical taps (1 original + 3 new).

Time taken by 4 taps to fill the remaining half = Time taken by 1 tap ÷ 4 = 3 ÷ 4 hours = 45 minutes.

Total time = 3 hours + 45 minutes = 3 hours 45 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours 45 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM = 6 units.

⇒ Efficiency of 1 tap = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Time taken by 1 tap to fill half the tank (3 units) = 3 ÷ 1 = 3 hours.

⇒ Remaining work to be done = 6 − 3 = 3 units.

⇒ Now, 3 more similar taps are opened. Total taps operating = 1 + 3 = 4 taps.

⇒ Combined efficiency of 4 taps = 4 × 1 = 4 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken to complete the remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency = 3 ÷ 4 hours.

⇒ Converting into minutes = (3 ÷ 4) × 60 = 45 minutes.

⇒ Total time taken to fill the tank completely = 3 hours + 45 minutes = 3 hours 45 min.

Pipes & Cisterns Net Work

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B fills it in y hours, their combined 1 hour work is (1/x + 1/y).

Efficiency of Multiple Identical Sources

When n identical taps are opened simultaneously, their combined efficiency becomes n times the efficiency of a single tap, effectively reducing the time required to 1/n.

Work Equivalence

Total Work = Number of identical workers (or taps) × Time taken × Efficiency. This is a direct application of the unitary method in Time & Work.

questions.question: Pipe A is 3 times faster than pipe B. Both pipes together fill a tank in 36 min. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A is 3 times faster than pipe B. Both pipes together fill a tank in 36 min.

**Formula used:**

Let the time taken by pipe B alone to fill the tank be B minutes.

Then, time taken by pipe A alone to fill the tank = B/3 minutes.

If both pipes together fill the tank in 36 minutes, then their combined rate is 1 tank per 36 minutes.

**Calculations:**

Rate of pipe B = 1/B tanks per minute

Rate of pipe A = 1/(B/3) = 3/B tanks per minute

Combined rate = 1/36 tanks per minute

⇒ 1/B + 3/B = 1/36

⇒ (1 + 3)/B = 1/36

⇒ 4/B = 1/36

⇒ B = 4 × 36 = 144 minutes

Time taken by pipe A alone to fill the tank = B/3

⇒ Time taken by pipe A alone = 144/3 = 48 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

Work done = Rate × Time

Efficiency of A = 15 L/h

Efficiency of B = 12 L/h

Efficiency of C = 10 L/h

15 + 12 - 10 = 17 liters per hour

Work Done in First 4 Hours

Work done in 4 hours: 17 × 4 = 68 liters

Remaining capacity of the tank:

120 - 68 = 52 liters

Work Done After Closing Pipe A

12 - 10 = 2 liters per hour

Time Required to Fill Remaining Tank = 52 / 2 = 26 hours

The remaining part of the tank will be filled in 26 hours.

**Given:**

B is used for half the time, and A and B together for the other half.

Combined work rate: If pipe A fills a tank in 'a' minutes and pipe B fills the same tank in 'b' minutes, then together they fill the tank in (a × b) / (a + b) minutes.

⇒ 2400 / 100 = 24 minutes

B is used for t/2 minutes, and A and B together for t/2 minutes.

Fraction filled by B = (t/2) / 40 = t/80

Fraction filled by A and B = (t/2) / 24 = t/48

⇒ 8t = 240

⇒ t = 240 / 8 = 30 minutes

**∴ It will take 30 minutes to fill the tanker.**

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively. Both the pipes are opened together but after 4 minutes, pipe A is turned off. What is the total time required to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 15 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the tank = 20 minutes

Both pipes are opened together for 4 minutes, then Pipe A is turned off.

**Formula used:**

Work done per minute = (Total capacity / Time taken)

**Calculation:**

LCM of 15 and 20 = 60 (Assuming tank capacity = 60 units)

Efficiency of Pipe A = 60 / 15 = 4 units/min

Efficiency of Pipe B = 60 / 20 = 3 units/min

Work done by both pipes in 4 minutes:

(4 × 4) + (3 × 4) = 16 + 12 = 28 units

Remaining work = 60 - 28 = 32 units

Now, only Pipe B is working, so time required to fill 32 units:

Time = 32 / 3 = 10(2)/(3) minutes = 10 minutes 40 seconds

Total time required = 4 minutes + 10 minutes 40 seconds = 14 minutes 40 seconds

**∴ The total time required to fill the tank is 14 minutes 40 seconds.**

⇒ 56 / 1 = 56 hours

**∴ The leak will completely empty the cistern in 56 hours.**

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 24 minutes, respectively, and a waste pipe can empty 3 gallons per minute. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 15 minutes. The capacity of the tank is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 24 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can empty 3 gallons per minute. 

 All three pipes working together can fill the tank in 15 minutes. 

Formula used:

Capacity = Time × Efficiency

Calculation:

Let total capacity = LCM[20, 24, 15] = 120 units

E(1st Pipe) = 120/20 = 6

E(2nd Pipe) = 120/24 = 5 

E(All three Pipes) = 120/15= 8 [∵ Capacity = Time × Efficiency]

3rd Pipe = E(All three Pipes) - E(1st Pipe) - E(2nd Pipe)

⇒ 3rd Pipe = 8 - 6 - 5 = - 3 units 

[negative as 3rd Pipe is a waste pipe]

∴ 3rd Pipe empties 3 units every minute

According to the question,

3 units = 3 gallons.

Thus, Capacity of tank = (120/3) × 3 = 120 gallons

∴ Capacity of the tank is 120 gallons.
